A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SCOPE-Gen research. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices are readable and support comparison, including matching material moved or renamed in v2.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendices E–F report original calibration-efficiency, runtime, prediction-set, admissibility, and qualitative results on four tasks.

after.justification: Section 5 and Appendices F–H retain original experiments and add configuration comparisons, admissibility-level evaluations, and held-out admissibility estimates.

M1.justification: Appendix D.1 adds config. 2, which retains only the diversity filter and adds a prediction-set count penalty with gamma_d = 0.1 to its update. The original procedure remains as config. 1; Algorithms 1–3 are unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate TriviaQA question answering, MIMIC-CXR report generation, CNN/DM summarization, and MOSES-based molecular graph extension. The added analyses use these same tasks. Human-expert evaluation remains a proposed application, not an added study.

E2.justification: Table 2 adds SCOPE-Gen config. 2 as a compared variant on MIMIC-CXR and CNN/DM. CLM, CLM reduced max, generation-only SCOPE-Gen, and flipped-filter SCOPE-Gen remain. Config. 1 matches the earlier standard SCOPE-Gen.

E3.justification: Appendix F.2 adds quantitative evaluations at alpha = 0.35 and 0.4. Appendix H adds a held-out assessment using calibration sizes 300, 600, and 1200 with 300 test cases. The stated max-score gamma changes from 0.3 in v1 E.2 to 0.1 in v2 F.2; unchanged original result values do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: V1 already examined non-conformity scores, filter order, filter removal, and MIMIC-CXR calibration size. V2 substantially extends this analysis with the penalized diversity-only variant, systematic admissibility-level comparisons, and post-calibration conditional admissibility checks across all four tasks in Appendix H.

E5.justification: V2 newly identifies a cross-validation-like procedure for the Figure 3 histograms and explicitly describes conditional, unbiased held-out estimation in Appendix H. The existing 300-repeat and standard-deviation reporting remains unchanged. Appendix H does not explicitly define its reported ± quantities.

E6.justification: Table 1 and the original Table 2 numerical entries are retained, while Table 2 and Appendix H add substantial results. For example, at alpha = 0.3 with sum scoring on MIMIC-CXR, new config. 2 reports set size 5.839 and 5.216 queries, versus config. 1's 7.390 and 4.214: smaller sets with more checks. Results at additional alpha levels are new conditions, not same-setting improvements.

T1.justification: Appendix B adds an explicit empirical-quantile definition, including the infinity convention for levels above one. Appendix H states conditional unbiasedness of its held-out estimator. The existing admissibility definitions, Markov factorization, and proof relating learn-then-test to conformal admissibility are retained.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: sequential greedy filtering provides admissibility control with fewer calibration queries and lower computational complexity, demonstrated on language and molecular tasks.

C2.justification: V2 adds inference-cost limitations and possible sampling-based mitigations in Appendix I, explains why model performance and sampling limits restrict smaller alpha values, and offers threshold-estimation variance as an explanation for generation-only set sizes. The earlier data-splitting and learn-then-test limitations are preserved after relocation.

D1.justification: V2 replaces the anonymized-supplement and promised future release statement with a named GitHub repository. Appendix D.1 documents config. 2's two-stage setup and penalty coefficient. These provide additional access and implementation information; repository availability was not independently checked.

R1.justification: Section 6 adds positioning against multiple-choice conformal prediction, long-form subclaim-filtering guarantees, and hallucination detection without distribution-free guarantees. Appendix I adds references on diverse sampling. These extend the research context while retaining the central comparisons with CLM and cascaded conformal filtering.

P1.justification: Most existing prose remains intact. V2 makes local wording and explanatory edits, updates affiliations and publication headers, adds acknowledgements, and moves Discussion & Limitations from the main text to Appendix I. Appendix headings and cross-references are updated accordingly.

P2.justification: Table 2 substantially expands its display structure through nested alpha/non-conformity groups, additional configuration rows, and continuation headers. Appendix H adds four dataset-specific calibration-size-by-alpha result blocks. Figures 1–3 and Table 1 retain their designs, with limited caption and placement changes.

improvement.justification: V2 strengthens evidence about the efficiency–set-size tradeoff through broader parameter comparisons and post-calibration checks, while improving code-access information and explaining applicability limits. These are useful incremental gains over v1's retained core results. Their value is tempered by the unexplained max-score gamma revision and undefined ± quantities in Appendix H, which limit the clarity of the added reporting.
